newsitem.title: USA: Amoco Virginia refinery unit damaged in fire.
newsitem.headline: Amoco Virginia refinery unit damaged in fire.

text.p: Amoco Corp said Tuesday that a furnace at the desulfurisation unit in the company's Yorktown, Virginia refinery which was damaged in a small fire last week was still in repair but operational changes had been made to minimise the impact on production.
Refinery spokesman Mike Brien said Amoco will meet customer demand despite the damage. "We have adequate inventories and supplies to meet our demand. There has been no interruption," he said.
The fire broke out last Tuesday evening in the furnace of the unit, which removes sulfur from heating oil.
Environmental regulators meanwhile said the fire was put out in 20 minutes and created insignificant air pollution.
"The fire was all contained with 20 minutes," said Dick Craft, compliance manager in the Air Division of the State of Virginia Department of Environmental Quality.
He would not give the unit's capacity, citing company policy.
He said, however, production at the refinery was at normal levels. The refinery has a 50,000 barrel per day capacity.
